name: kamishibai
description: Turn a web page into a video — every frame a pure function of its time, so capture is reproducible and parallel.

paragraphs: Turn any web page into a video. kamishibai only seeks the page to each moment and captures it. A mechanism, not a framework. How you draw — React, plain DOM, canvas, WebGL — is up to you.
Rendered by kamishibai from site/demo/reel.ts: plain DOM, the one contract, and the Lexicon's drawings. (full mp4)

kamishibai turns any web page (DOM, canvas, anything) into a video by seeking to each moment and capturing a still, then assembling the stills with ffmpeg. Because every frame is a pure function of its time, capture is reproducible — in a pinned environment, any order of frames gives the same video — and trivially parallelisable across several pages of a headless Chrome.
features: 🧩 Minimal. One contract: the page exposes window.kamishibai = { meta, seek }. No framework to adopt, no editor.
🎨 Draw it any way. React, plain DOM, canvas, three.js: anything a browser can show. The React helpers are optional.

⚡ Edit, then render only what changed. --incremental captures again only the frames an edit touched. After one heading edit in an 86-second reel, it rendered again in 25 s, where Remotion took 48 s and HyperFrames 51 s…
🔁 Reproducible and parallel. In a pinned environment, any order of frames gives the same video, so the frames are captured on several pages at once.
🔊 Sound included. Audio clips, background music with ducking, TTS narration and frame-accurate video clips.
